items.title: No manager handoff until the requisite flows are built, implemented AND verified working
items.observed: Operator-directed 2026-09-02: "I don't want to handoff before we are at least 200% certain that the requisite flows and merchanisms are built, implmented, and verified working correctly". Also, earlier the same hour: "i don't want to hand off before we're ready - that's why I keep asking you instead of telling you." So handoff readiness is the OPERATOR'S call and handoff_check's readiness=ready is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT.
items.root_cause: handoff_check grades whether a SUCCESSOR CAN SEE the state -- registry, lease, checklist, open-PR rows. It says nothing about whether the MECHANISMS WORK. Those are different questions and this repo's whole vocabulary exists to keep them apart: landed_unproven is not done, a merge is not a deploy, and a deploy is not an observation.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: THE BAR, STATED AS OBSERVATIONS SO IT IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN A FEELING. Each names what would settle it, and a green test settles NONE of them: (1) DECISION ROUND-TRIP ON CLAUDEBOT -- a tap on ClaudeBot producing a work_decision_transit row, then that same request grading `committed` on /api/bot/work/decisions with the answer block on main. Already PROVEN on the TRADER bot (10:11:42Z prompt, 10:16:36Z tap, submitted_by telegram); the ClaudeBot leg is not. [!] CORRECTED 2026-09-02 BY MI-58, AND THE MANAGER'S PREMISE WAS FALSE. The manager told MI-58 that 'once TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is set, the fallback can never fire' and used that to argue for KEEPING the trader-bot fallback rather than making it fail-closed. WRONG: answerable_route() requires a live HEARTBEAT, not merely a token, so if ict-claude-decision-bot.service dies or is masked, decisions land on the trader bot again WITH THE SECRET SET. The fallback is PERMANENT, not a pre-secret window. The decision to keep it may still be right on its own merits -- a wrong chat is a noise complaint, holding every prompt is an outage -- but the reason given for it was not. [!] SO SETTING THE SECRET IS NOT THE POST-DEPLOY CHECK. Read /api/diag/log_file?name=telegram_poll_claude and `destination` in the sweep stats. 'Decisions still arrive' is NOT evidence the move happened -- that is precisely what the fallback produces. (2) /status AND /decisions -- the operator types each and gets a correct reply, ON CLAUDEBOT. #10793 is held as a draft precisely so this cannot be satisfied on the wrong bot. (3) PUSH-BACK TO THE ASKING SESSION (MI-60, #10788) -- a committed decision reaching the session that asked, without a minted token. B is not done when the Routine EXISTS; it is done when something WATCHES that it FIRED (list_triggers.last_run), because two Routines on this account were enabled and never once fired. (4) THE WORK STORE -- a COLD session, not pointed there by its prompt, acting on the readout or the cycle priority and citing where it read it. (5) NO WORK IS LOST (Phase E) -- demonstrated BY KILLING A SESSION MID-WORK, not asserted from a test. Nobody has killed one. (6) THE DAILY DIGEST -- one run with event=schedule. A workflow_dispatch run is not a cron run.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] THE MANAGER IS THE WRONG JUDGE OF (4) AND CANNOT CLEAR IT. A cold observation is by definition made by a session that was not told, and this manager built or dispatched most of these. Record WHICH session made each observation. [!] AND DO NOT LET THIS ROW BECOME A REASON NEVER TO HAND OFF. It is a bar, not a veto: if a mechanism turns out to be unverifiable rather than merely unverified, that is a finding to report to the operator, not a condition to wait out forever.

items.title: The most privileged role in the system has no skill, so every manager re-derives the job from prose and repeats the same mistakes
items.spawn_when: After MI-66, or in the same session if scope allows. Both are enactment of the operating-layer inventory.
items.observed: Operator, 2026-09-02: 'how do we ensure that you future manager session don't make the same mistake?' MEASURED in answering it: 32 skills exist and NOT ONE is a manager role pack. The role that merges, deploys, spawns sessions, holds the lease and answers to the operator is the only significant role with no pack. Everything a manager knows arrives as prose -- CLAUDE.md, a sweep-trigger prompt, and whatever the previous manager wrote in a checklist note.
items.root_cause: DOCUMENTATION HAS ALREADY BEEN TRIED AND MEASURABLY FAILED, and that is the whole argument for this row. The CI-never-fired trap is stated VERBATIM in CLAUDE.md ('if such a commit lands last your PR shows ZERO checks and is blocked, not green -- push an ordinary commit after, to arm CI'). The manager session of 2026-09-02 had read that line and hit the trap THREE TIMES the same afternoon (#10793, #10795, #10789). Restating a rule that is known and still broken is not a fix; this repo's own F4 says a repeated mistake becomes an executable check or it is not a lesson.
items.scope: A `manager` skill carrying (a) the loop -- lease heartbeat, read the registers, merge one at a time re-verifying between, review before un-drafting, spawn through the registry -- and (b) an EXECUTABLE PREFLIGHT rather than a list of reminders. The preflight must include, at minimum, the four failures measured on 2026-09-02: 1. BEFORE trusting `total_count: 0`, read mergeable_state AND the head commit's AUTHOR -- a bot-authored head means CI never fired (BL-20260902-BOARD-POST-RELAY-SILENTLY-KILLS-CI-ON-THE-PR-OF-ANY-SESSION-THAT-FOLLOWS-THE-PROTOCOL...). 2. BEFORE landing a register-touching manager PR, check what sibling PRs it will re-conflict; the manager is the highest-frequency writer to those files (BL-20260902-FIVE-MONOLITHIC-JSON-REGISTERS-RECONFLICT-EVERY-SIBLING-PR-ON-EVERY-MERGE...). 3. BEFORE blocking work on a claim about live state, PROBE it. The 2026-09-02 manager blocked the ClaudeBot work on 'TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is unset', asserted from a doc row dated the previous day, against the operator's own contrary sighting (MI-65). 4. BEFORE a read-append-write on any register, confirm the file round-trips; OPEN-ITEMS.json does not (BL-20260902-OPEN-ITEMS-IS-THE-ONE-REGISTER-NO-APPEND-HELPER-PROTECTS). 5. F6 -- REFUSE TO PROCEED when the count of unnotified autonomous actions since the last ping exceeds a stated threshold. This is the fifth item and arguably the first in importance: F6 is the CONDITION the autonomy grant rests on, and on 2026-09-02 a manager merged 5 PRs, dispatched 4 sessions, held a PR to block a deploy and made a fallback design call across ~8 hours while sending ZERO pings -- the operator noticed before the manager did. The class of action most worth reporting is exactly the class that is silent, because merge_pull_request / update_pull_request / create_session / fire_trigger are MCP calls with no notification hop, while the narrow VM system-actions DO carry one. BL-20260902-THE-MANAGERS-HIGH-IMPACT-ACTIONS-BYPASS-EVERY-PATH-THAT-NOTIFIES.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: An executable preflight the manager RUNS, not a section it reads -- the `handoff_check.py` shape, which already refuses `ready` rather than grading a soft pass, and which is the one manager mechanism that has worked reliably today. Every item above is checkable from a script.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] A SKILL IS STILL PROSE UNTIL THE CHECKS EXIST. Writing a `manager` SKILL.md and stopping there would reproduce exactly the failure this row documents -- and would be harder to see, because the role pack would LOOK like the fix. The deliverable is the checks; the skill is where they are invoked from. [!] AND IT INHERITS MI-66's FINDING: no role pack references the operating layer at all, so a new manager pack must point at the work store, the readout and the caps rather than the pre-2026-09-01 world of three backlogs and DUE.md. Writing it against the old world would add a 33rd skill with the same gap.
items.landed_unproven_because: #10808 MERGED 2026-09-02 (67cfb8be). ⚠️ TWO OF THE THREE MECHANISMS WORK AND THE THIRD CANNOT. The manager VERIFIED spawn_gate.py on both controls itself -- out-of-priority exits 3, in-priority exits 0. But queue_latency.py grades `unknown` PERMANENTLY: its verdict needs a live list_sessions read and CI holds no mcp__* tools. Honest, and not yet a guard. MI-73 owns closing that.

items.title: A rebase or merge of main arms auto-merge on a claude/** branch, because the push diff includes everything main changed
items.observed: Found and filed by MI-58. claude-pr-automerge.yml still carries the LEGACY shared marker `.github/pr-automerge-request` in its paths: filter and that file is still in the tree, so any claude/** branch that merges or rebases main touches the path and is UN-DRAFTED AND ARMED having asked for nothing. [!] THIS EXPLAINS AN OBSERVATION THE MANAGER MADE AND COULD NOT ACCOUNT FOR: on #10795 the manager noted that github-actions[bot] un-drafted the PR and enabled auto-merge 'without a marker file in my diff' and flagged it as odd. This is the cause. The manager had the symptom; MI-58 had the mechanism.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Remove the legacy shared path from the workflow's paths: filter so ONLY the per-request .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt opt-in arms it. That per-request path is already the documented convention and its README records why the shared marker was wrong.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] DELETING A HOLD FILE IS NOT THE FIX. A test-file hold WAS deleted on 2026-09-02 (correctly, for an unrelated reason) and could be mistaken for remediation. The mechanism is untouched.
items.note: #10810 reviewed by the manager and ARMED 2026-09-02, not yet merged. Its central finding is that removing the legacy shared marker FIXES NOTHING ON ITS OWN -- measured across the three misfires, that path appears in ZERO of them; what matched is the GLOB, because any branch merging main drags other branches' request files into its push diff. The real fix is a REQUEST GATE proving THIS branch asked, plus never un-drafting a PR the workflow did not create.

items.title: Decision PRESENTATION on ClaudeBot: options as a readable list, and real multiple choice
items.tier: 2 (touches the Telegram bridge; no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps)
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, EXPLICITLY not urgent: 'Also not urgent, but something that I do want us to have ... somewhere in our work plan.'
items.observed: Operator, on the live decision prompt: 'the point with the buttons is that it's very shortened, a little cut off ... maybe there's more of a list and I can click the options, maybe some would be multiple choice. I think that button is a good first step, but probably not the end of where this design needs to go.' So the ASK half of the decision round-trip works and its PRESENTATION is the limit.
items.⚠️_the_truncation_is_the_LABEL_not_the_c: DO NOT go looking for a callback_data size bug -- it is already solved and re-solving it would waste the session. `callback_data` is 26 bytes FIXED (`wdec:<12 hex>:<8 hex>`) against Telegram's 64-byte cap, and it carries a DIGEST of the option KEY, deliberately never a positional index. What the operator sees cut off is the BUTTON LABEL, which Telegram renders narrow and elides. Those are different layers.

the_shape_to_build.1_options_as_a_numbered_list_in_the_MESS: Put the full option text in the message body as a numbered list -- where there is room for it -- and reduce each button to its number. The body is not width-constrained the way a button is, so the option a person is choosing between becomes readable without touching the callback contract at all. This is the cheap half and it is probably most of the win.
the_shape_to_build.2_multiple_choice_is_NOT_one_press: [!] A single inline keyboard press submits ONE value, so multi-select is not a formatting change -- it needs a TOGGLE keyboard: each tap flips an option's mark and re-renders the keyboard, and an explicit Submit sends the set. That means holding PARTIAL, UNSUBMITTED state between taps, which the current design deliberately does not have. Decide where that state lives BEFORE building it; a half-submitted answer that looks submitted is the forward-failure the transit contract exists to refuse.
the_shape_to_build.3_free_text_is_still_a_separate_step: Unchanged and deliberately not half-built: inline buttons cannot carry arbitrary text. A request declaring no options is still SENT (so a blocking question is never invisible) and says plainly that it needs an answer on the SPA or in the repo.

items.what_must_not_regress: The four never-collapsed answer states (`not_submitted`/`in_transit`/`committed`/`unreadable`); the option token staying a KEY DIGEST rather than an index (an index silently records a different answer if the object is reordered between send and tap); the fail-closed write gate; and the confirmation continuing to read 'Submitted -- NOT yet decided'.
items.why_deferred: P1 is the handoff capability and P2 is the overhaul implementation. This is a UX improvement to a channel that already works end-to-end -- the round-trip was observed complete on 2026-09-02. The operator said not urgent and this records that as a decision, not as an oversight.

items.title: The daily manager cadence: day session → declared wrap → night manager → morning brief
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, as the shape the handoff should take
items.⚠️_THIS_SUPERSEDES_THE_MANAGERS_OWN_FRAM: The manager reported that `open_prs` completeness is POINT-IN-TIME and concluded 'a handoff has to be taken in a QUIET WINDOW, or the check needs a bounded tolerance.' That framing is PASSIVE -- it waits for a quiet moment that a busy repo never reliably offers. The operator's answer is ACTIVE and is better: you do not wait for a quiet window, you CREATE one, by declaring per thread which PR is the LAST one before the manager moves on. Do not re-derive the tolerance idea from the old framing; the boundary is declared, not awaited.

the_cycle.1_morning: The day STARTS WITH A PING — a daily brief into a NEW manager session. ⚠️ The brief must carry WHAT WAS DONE OVERNIGHT and what was wrapped up after the operator went to bed. Operator: 'by the [brief] in the morning, I want that to include what was done overnight and what was wrapped up after I went to bed, so that I know where I'm starting off from.' A brief that only describes the new day's plan fails its purpose.
the_cycle.3_wrap: The operator SAYS when they are going to bed. That is the trigger, not a clock. The manager then produces a RAPID WRAP PLAN: (a) the LAST PR for each thread; (b) confirmation that NO Tier-3 decision is left dangling -- and any that is gets LOGGED FOR THE NEXT DAY rather than carried in a session's head; (c) close everything down.
the_cycle.4_night: The manager SETS OFF THE NIGHT SESSION ITSELF, scoped by HOW MUCH TIME IT HAS until the morning brief. Night work is deliberately the low-operator-dependency kind: backlog items and UI, 'things that are less important and need less of me, and very easy to run without me.' ⚠️ NOTHING TIER-3 AND NOTHING NEEDING A DECISION goes to the night session -- it cannot get an answer.

items.the_last_PR_per_thread_rule: ⚠️ READ WHAT THE OPERATOR RULED OUT, not just what they asked for. They explicitly did NOT ask that entire MILESTONES be finished before a handoff: 'it just means that for each thread of workflow, we need to decide what the last PR for each manager is gonna be before we move on, and that needs to be documented clearly so that we can make sure that we're sticking to that.' So the unit is a DECLARED TERMINAL PR PER THREAD, documented in advance and held to -- not milestone completion, which would block every handoff indefinitely.
items.what_this_needs_built: Not yet designed, and deliberately not designed here: where the per-thread terminal PR is DECLARED (OPEN-PRS.json rows already carry a thread via checklist_item, so this may be a field rather than a new register); how the morning brief is GENERATED from the overnight record rather than written by hand; and whether the night session's scope is bounded by a stated deadline it can read. Operator also raised timers/pings for start-and-finish awareness -- worth a design pass, not a guess.
items.⚠️_honest_precondition: The operator's own read: 'it sounds like we still have a lot of [work] here to get [addressed] so that we're able to do an actual reliable handoff.' This item does NOT claim the cadence is achievable today. handoff_check.py still reads not_ready more often than ready on a busy repo.
items.⚠️_CORRECTION_THE_MANAGER_MADE_TO_ITSELF: THE NIGHT HOP NEEDS NO NEW MECHANISM, and the first version of this row said it did. It read: 'the night-manager hop depends on a fresh-session-per-fire routine gated on the lease, which does not exist.' That is FALSE for the flow the operator actually described, which has the MANAGER setting the night session off directly -- 'set off the night manager session yourself' -- and `create_session` is proven to do exactly that (MI-73 was spawned with it on 2026-09-02). Overstating a blocker is not a safe error: it invites a session to build a routine nobody needs and to treat tonight's handoff as impossible when it is not.
items.what_ACTUALLY_needs_a_mechanism: ⚠️ DECIDED 2026-09-02 — THE MORNING WAKE IS MANUAL, AND THIS IS AN ANSWER, NOT A GAP. Operator, verbatim: 'There's [no] new need for a timer or a trigger for the morning manager. I will do that manually. I will get the daily brief. I will read it, and then I will use it as the beginning of a prompt, which I'll also add my notes to, to set off the manager session for that day. So that doesn't need to be set off automatically. I wanna be there at the beginning.' So: NO cron routine, NO create_new_session_on_fire, NO lease-gated auto-spawn. Do not build one, and do not re-open this as an oversight -- the operator being present at the start of the day is a DELIBERATE choice, and automating it would remove the point.
items.⚠️_the_self_bound_sweep_limit_is_still_r: Unchanged by the correction above: the manager sweep re-armed 2026-09-02T15:20Z is SELF-BOUND and dies with its session. That is a genuine gap for a manager that DIES mid-day -- it is simply not the gap the night handoff has, because the night handoff is deliberate and the manager is alive to perform it.
items.⚠️_what_the_manual_wake_does_NOT_remove: THE BRIEF ITSELF IS STILL A DELIVERABLE AND IS STILL UNBUILT. The operator says 'I will GET the daily brief' -- they are the trigger, not the author. Something must PRODUCE a brief that carries what happened overnight, and that is precisely the half their stated reason depends on: 'so that I know where I'm starting off from.' Separating these two matters, because the wake being settled makes it easy to read the whole morning end as settled. The wake is decided; the brief is open. Most likely the NIGHT session's closing output is the brief, which would make it a night-session deliverable rather than a new mechanism -- but that is a proposal, not a decision, and nobody has built it.

items.title: A notifications menu per bot: choose WHICH notifications, and a CADENCE for the periodic ones
items.tier: 2 (Telegram bridge + a stored per-chat preference; no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps)
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, EXPLICITLY for the backlog: 'a further idea, though, that I do want us to backlog as well ... so that we eventually get to it.'
items.observed: Operator: 'in the menu for each of the bots for there to be an option for notifications, which would then pull up a list of the notifications, and I could choose which ones. And for the ones that are periodic, there should be some choices for cadence -- hourly, daily, weekly, maybe once, twice, three times daily, depending on what kind of thing it is.' Raised alongside making the work digest hourly, which is the manual version of exactly this control.
items.⚠️_HALF_OF_THIS_ALREADY_EXISTS_AND_LOST_: DO NOT BUILD THE 'WHICH' HALF FROM SCRATCH -- measure it first. A per-kind subscription model is already shipped and has been since M12: `GET /api/bot/devices/event-kinds` serves the canonical taxonomy from `src.runtime.mobile_push.event_kinds` (kind/label/description/in_flight) precisely so a client need not mirror the list, and `PATCH /api/bot/devices/{id}/subscriptions` stores a per-device choice as `null|[kinds]|{kind:bool}`. It was built for the Android app's Notifications screen -- and the Android app was RETIRED from the live feed on 2026-09-01, with `device_tokens` measured EMPTY (0 registered devices). So this is a mechanism that is written, works, and now has no reader: the `provenance-consumer-guard` shape one level up, the same shape MI-70 found with the `Claude-Session:` commit trailer. The honest framing of this item is RE-POINT AN EXISTING TAXONOMY AT TELEGRAM, plus build the genuinely new half.

what_is_genuinely_new.cadence_per_kind: The existing model is a BOOLEAN per kind (on/off). Cadence is a third value and the taxonomy has no field for it. Note the operator's own distinction -- 'depending on what kind of thing it is' -- so cadence is not universal: an EVENT (a decision ready, an incident) is immediate-or-nothing and a cadence choice on it is meaningless, while a DIGEST (the work digest, the daily roll-up) is exactly where cadence belongs. The taxonomy therefore needs to say which kinds are cadence-BEARING, or the menu will offer 'weekly' on an alert.
what_is_genuinely_new.per_CHAT_not_per_DEVICE: `device_tokens` is keyed on an FCM token. Telegram has no such token; the natural key is the chat/bot pair. Whether that is a new table or a widened one is the first design question, and it is the one that decides how much of the existing model is reusable.
what_is_genuinely_new.a_menu_is_stateful: Same constraint as MI-71: one inline press submits one value, so a multi-select preferences screen is a TOGGLE keyboard plus an explicit Save, which means holding partial unsubmitted state. The two items share this problem and should probably share its solution -- do not solve it twice, differently.

items.⚠️_what_must_not_become_switchable: A preferences menu that can silence anything is a way to turn off an alarm and forget. The severity-band rule stands: a P0 (money at risk) page is NOT a preference. Whatever this ships with, the CRITICAL/unprotected-position class must remain unmutable, or this feature becomes the desensitized-alarm P1 with a UI in front of it.
items.why_deferred: P1 is the handoff capability, P2 the overhaul implementation. The operator asked for it to be backlogged, not built, and the immediate need it came with -- an hourly work digest -- was satisfied directly by a cron change.

items.title: The manager watcher is BLIND by construction — give it a sensor that can actually see
items.observed: Of the three mechanisms MI-68 built to watch the manager (merged #10808), TWO WORK and the third cannot. `spawn_gate.py` was verified by the manager on BOTH controls -- out-of-priority object exits 3, in-priority exits 0. But `queue_latency.py`, the one aimed at the manager sitting on a blocked queue, reports `unknown` PERMANENTLY: its verdict needs a live `list_sessions` read, that is an mcp__* tool, and CI holds no MCP tools. It refuses to substitute SESSIONS.json's stale `last_observed`, which is correct -- that register has been measured incomplete twice.
items.why_it_matters: This is the failure that cost the most on 2026-09-02: four sub-sessions sat IDLE and BLOCKED on the manager for up to 142 minutes while the manager asserted they held work. It is also the operator's core ask -- 'actual guards and mechanisms in the repo/vm themselves that watch the manager and enforce the rules on him.' A permanently-`unknown` watcher is honest but is not yet that guard.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST_not_assume: The same failure has an MCP-FREE PROXY that GitHub Actions can see with nothing but its own GITHUB_TOKEN: a PR green/mergeable/unmerged and ageing; a `needs_action` posted with nothing since; a board `▶️ START` with no `✅ DONE`, ageing; an `in_flight` checklist item whose owner's branch has had no push for N hours. ⚠️ THE MANAGER BELIEVES THIS AND HAS NOT PROVEN IT. If the proxy is weaker than it looks, a STATED BOUNDARY is the better deliverable -- which is exactly what MI-68 delivered on queue_latency and why its work merged.
items.what_must_not_regress: (a) Do NOT delete or weaken the `unknown` path -- `quiet`/`escalate`/`unknown` must never collapse, because 'we could not look' and 'nothing is waiting' are opposite facts. (b) It must NOT be invokable by the manager: MI-68's own measurement is that every mechanism the manager had to choose to run went unused, and every mechanism that stood in the way worked. (c) Never page on activity, only on a state that is actually stuck, rate-limited per class -- 202 of 376 CRITICAL rows in one measured window here were a single un-latched alarm.
items.⚠️_a_cron_is_not_evidence_of_a_run: work-digest.yml's own header records a scheduled workflow in this repo firing ~4h50m LATE and once instead of daily. Whatever carries this must make its own liveness checkable.
items.⚠️_outcome: DIED BLOCKED, WORK LOST. post_turn_summary: 'blocked on permission classifier; auto-mode denied add_repo x2 and git push x3'. It never pushed a branch, so ~$10 of work is unrecoverable -- exactly the loss MI-70 demonstrated by killing a session. Two manager wake attempts did not clear it: the denial is its session's permission classifier, which the manager cannot change from outside. SUPERSEDED BY MI-77, respawned with an explicit source_url (which this session's context lacked) and instructed to push within its first minutes. [!] THE MANAGER'S FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: it told MI-73 the cause was an omitted source_url, then found MI-75 had a source it never passed and MI-76 acquired one late -- sources attach ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so 'no sources' reads as a defect when it is often just a timing artifact.

items.title: Phase E: prove no work is lost by actually killing a session mid-work
items.landed_unproven_because: #10812 and #10820 both MERGED 2026-09-02. ⚠️ THE REAPER HAS STILL NEVER BEEN OBSERVED RUNNING TO COMPLETION, and #10820 is why that matters: the version merged in #10812 pushed straight to PROTECTED main (GH006), so every scheduled run would have reaped correctly and RECORDED NOTHING -- a frozen ledger reading exactly like a quiet week. The owner found that itself, after merge, and fixed it via .github/actions/commit-to-main with verify-merged: true.
items.the_ruling_it_carries: ⚠️ PHASE E DOES NOT CLOSE ON THIS. The kill was RUN and demonstrated a PARTIAL loss -- 'killing a session loses everything it had not pushed, and nothing it had' -- which CONTRADICTS the object's done-condition ('loses nothing'). Manager ruled 2026-09-02: do NOT amend the condition to match the result (that fits the bar to the outcome) and do NOT leave 'loses nothing' standing (unachievable -- the loss is in a dead container no reaper can reach). BOUND it instead, and keep Phase E open until a successor object exists for PUSH CADENCE, which is the only lever that moves the number.
items.⚠️_do_not_merge: `claude/mi70-kill-subject` must NEVER be merged. It is the EVIDENCE for the kill demonstration and holds a throwaway notes file.

items.title: The HANDOFF BRIEF — what a successor manager and the operator are handed, generated not written
items.why_this_is_the_last_P1_gap: The operator set the daily cadence and then decided BOTH hops are MANUAL -- the manager spawns the night session (create_session, proven), and the operator starts the morning one because 'I wanna be there at the beginning.' That CLOSED the wake question and left exactly one thing open: they say they will GET the daily brief. They are the TRIGGER, not the author, and NOTHING PRODUCES ONE.
items.acceptance_is_the_operators_own_words: 'by the [brief] in the morning, I want that to include what was done overnight and what was wrapped up after I went to bed, SO THAT I KNOW WHERE I'M STARTING OFF FROM.' A brief that renders but does not answer that fails, however well-formed it is.
items.two_consumers_and_it_is_an_open_question: (1) THE OPERATOR IN THE MORNING -- readable prose they paste as the opening of the next manager's prompt, carrying what happened overnight. (2) A SUCCESSOR MANAGER MID-DAY -- live state: checklist, in-flight sessions, open PRs with their operator decisions AND conditions, loud open-items, the lease, what is blocked and on what. The owner was told to ARGUE the choice rather than assume it.
items.⚠️_the_real_constraint_it_must_not_fake_: What MERGED is readable from git and the registers are readable, but WHAT A NIGHT SESSION CONCLUDED lives in get_session's post_turn_summary -- and mcp__* tools are unavailable to CI and to routine-fired turns. So the brief is probably a CLOSE-OUT DELIVERABLE the night manager runs before it ends, not a cron. The owner must decide that honestly and say which.
items.what_must_not_regress: GENERATED never hand-written (a hand-written brief dies with its session, which is the failure Phase E exists for); it must DECLARE what it could not read rather than silently omitting a register; and it must not flatten `landed_unproven` into `done` -- saying an item is finished when its effect was never observed actively misinforms the person starting the day.

items.title: The manager watcher that can actually see (MI-73 respawn)
items.why: Of MI-68's three manager-watching mechanisms, TWO WORK (spawn_gate verified by the manager on both controls) and queue_latency.py grades `unknown` PERMANENTLY because its verdict needs a live list_sessions read and CI holds no mcp__* tools. Honest, and not yet the guard the operator asked for.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: An MCP-free proxy visible to Actions with only GITHUB_TOKEN: a green/mergeable/UNMERGED PR ageing; a needs_action with nothing since; a board START with no DONE; an in_flight item whose owner's branch has had no push for N hours. ⚠️ THE MANAGER BELIEVES THIS AND HAS NOT PROVEN IT -- a stated boundary is the better deliverable if the proxy is weaker than it looks.
items.what_must_not_regress: Do not collapse quiet/escalate/unknown. Must NOT be manager-invokable (every mechanism the manager had to choose to run went unused; every one that stood in the way worked). Never page on activity. And a cron is not evidence of a run -- session-reaper.yml had FIVE failing runs before its first success because it pushed to protected main, so this must land through .github/actions/commit-to-main with verify-merged: true.

items.title: Drain the stalled draft queue — 5 of 5 branches conflict against a freshly fetched main
items.tier: 1 (conflict resolution on existing PRs; no order path)
items.why: Five open drafts from finished sessions -- #10794, #10793, #10776, #10748, #10694 -- all conflicting, oldest quiescent 20h and one automation PR 109.6h. MI-77's watcher flagged exactly this queue on its first run, which is the watcher confirming its own premise. Main merged THREE times in the 40 minutes I measured over (4f664aab -> 82edebd6 -> 002e0ab8), so each branch is strictly harder to land tomorrow than today.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: Contention is CONCENTRATED, not diffuse: scripts/ops/render_due_list.py conflicts in 2 of the 5 branches and scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py in 2. If that holds, the queue is blocked by two shared files rather than by five independent problems, and the merge ORDER matters more than the individual resolutions. NOT the register-header churn MI-76 diagnosed -- only one branch touches a register (DUE.json), so the merge driver from #10826 is not what unblocks this.
items.done_when: Each of the five is conflict-free with all three required checks green and STILL A DRAFT, or closed with a written reason handed to the manager rather than closed by the session. A merge ORDER is delivered naming which pairs re-conflict each other. Drafts are kept because the artifact cap is 4 concurrent non-draft PRs and the manager serializes.
items.note: MANAGER MEASUREMENT ERROR, recorded because it changed the conclusion in the OPTIMISTIC direction. My first scan ran `git fetch origin <branch>` per branch, which does NOT advance origin/main, so it graded against a stale base and read 4 of 6 conflicted WITH #10694 CLEAN. Against a freshly fetched main it is 5 of 5. I acted on the clean reading first -- started merging main into #10694 to arm its CI -- and the merge conflicted, which is how I caught it. A mergeability read is only as current as the base you fetched, and this one was reported before it was re-checked. || 2026-09-02T20:12Z MANAGER VERIFICATION, and its own summary is WRONG. MI-79 reports '5 draft PRs merged, all CI green'. THREE merged (#10794 18:48Z, #10694 18:49Z, #10793 18:53Z); #10776 and #10748 are STILL OPEN AND STILL DRAFT. The cause is me, not it: at ~18:57 I disabled auto-merge on both and returned them to draft as containment after #10793 merged itself, and MI-79 had no way to know. Its summary reports what it EXPECTED, which is exactly why a session's own claim is not evidence. ⚠️ NOT graded `done`: two of its five are unlanded and it flagged '4 issues for review' nobody has read. ⚠️ AND ONE OF THE THREE IT LANDED IS THE UNAUTHORISED #10793 -- resolving that PR's conflict is what let its pre-armed auto-merge fire. That is not MI-79's fault (it was told to resolve and keep drafts, and #10793 was already armed before it started) but it is the mechanism, and recording it as a clean landing would hide it.

items.title: The operator's ping cadence rides GitHub cron, and GitHub cron does not fire
items.why: The operator asked directly at 18:33Z: 'no pings for 3 hours?' -- and it was FOUR. Measured over the COMPLETE run history of work-digest.yml (total_count 3, a census not a page): three runs all day, at 00:19Z / 07:10Z / 14:33Z, ~7h apart against a declared 6x/day, and ONE OF THE THREE FAILED. The hourly cron went live at 16:22Z (#10815) and BOTH the 17:20Z and 18:20Z slots did not fire. The minutes match no declared offset, so GitHub is not late -- it is not honouring the schedule.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: NOT 'move it to a Routine' -- that is the manager's hypothesis and MI-80 is deliberately told not to inherit it. Three candidates to rule in or out with evidence: (a) GitHub deprioritises scheduled workflows on a busy repo; (b) the job's own shape -- budget 40 minutes because commit-to-main waits up to 30m for its auto-merge PR, with concurrency cancel-in-progress:false, so an hourly cadence and a 40-minute job OVERLAP BY DESIGN and that may be the whole story; (c) the right fix is not a new carrier at all but that a MISSED SLOT BECOMES VISIBLE -- today a missed digest and a quiet hour are indistinguishable. Contrast worth testing against: Claude Routines on the same account fire on time (the :26 sweep fired 54s late) while GitHub cron is hours off or absent.
items.done_when: The digest arrives on a cadence OBSERVED over at least 6 consecutive expected slots with the misses COUNTED rather than assumed, and a missed or FAILED run is itself surfaced. Moving the carrier is not sufficient on its own -- a new carrier must be measured against its declared slots the same way GitHub's was. A workflow_dispatch run is NOT evidence the cron works.
items.note: #10845 armed for auto-merge 20:54Z after the manager merged 15 commits of main into it (the branch had sat 15 behind with ZERO check runs fired -- not a conflict; merge-tree was clean with AND without the register driver). ⚠️ IT DOES NOT FIX THE OPERATOR'S MISSING PINGS and must not be read as doing so: work-digest.yml run #5 fired on event:schedule at 19:47Z, success, and the operator still received nothing. What it fixes is that a digest never QUEUED cannot be delivered. The delivery-marking defect is BL-20260902-PING-DELIVERY-IS-MARKED-ON-A-LOCAL-FILE-WRITE-SO-DELIVERED-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE. || [OBSERVED 2026-09-06 by session_01UaZ9boMDajiCZsjVkr4Fnz, Phase 1A observation sweep] THE PREMISE 'GitHub cron does not fire' IS CONTRADICTED BY TODAY'S EVIDENCE and is worth re-deciding rather than continuing to chase the push trigger. THREE independent carriers were observed landing on schedule: (1) docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json on origin/main reads generated_at 2026-09-06T05:58:56Z with trigger 'SCHEDULE' (not 'push') and run_url .../actions/runs/34015289993 -- so the Actions cron fired, and clause (1) of OI-20260902-DIGEST-MOVED-OFF-A-CRON, which requires trigger='push', is therefore still UNMET while the digest is nonetheless landing. Its last four commits are 2026-09-06 09:00:55, 07:42:49, 03:31:59 and 01:57:47 (+0300). (2) docs/claude/work/PR-QUEUE-WATCH.json has four 'auto' receipts in ~32h (#11095, #11061, #11030, #11005). (3) The VM-side systemd carrier is ALSO live -- see MI-80's sibling in OI-20260902-HOURLY-DIGEST-CARRIER: ict-work-digest.timer reads ACTIVE and /api/diag/log_file?name=work_digest_receipt shows outcome 'sent' at 2026-09-06T09:01:04Z. WHAT REMAINS TRUE: the quiet-window half is untouched -- a push-driven digest still cannot heartbeat while main is quiet -- and I could not confirm any run's EVENT directly (api.github.com HTTP 403, no Actions MCP tool), so 'trigger: schedule' in the committed receipt is the evidence, read from the artifact rather than the run history.

items.title: The overdue trainer row — observe it, and build the data-freshness alarm if one can be built
items.tier: 1 (trainer read; trainer VM is autonomous territory)
items.why: OI-20260829-TRAINER-IS-NOW-A-DECIDED-DEPENDENCY-AND-IS-UNMONITORED is FOUR days past a THREE-day cadence. The operator DECIDED on 2026-08-29 to keep the trainer for L2 order-flow capture -- a forward-only stream nothing can re-derive -- and the row records the disk at 92% with nothing watching. The row is loud and renders in the CLAUDE.md brief and was STILL not observed, which makes it a live instance of the failure OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION watches: the register surfaces it and nobody acts.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: The two halves are DIFFERENT FACTS and must not be collapsed. (1) OBSERVE -- what is the disk headroom, is the capture still writing, how stale is its newest data. (2) ALARM -- keyed on the DATA's freshness at the named path, NEVER on the unit's ActiveState, because a systemd unit can be `active` while writing nothing and a unit-state alarm would be green straight through the failure this watches. The row's own clears_when requires the alarm be SHOWN to fire against PLANTED staleness, not merely deployed.
items.done_when: The row's observation carries what was SEEN (verbatim, with the command) and verified_at is re-dated. The row clears only if the freshness alarm exists AND was shown to fire against planted staleness; otherwise it stays open with the reason. Disk headroom recovering on its own does NOT clear it -- the gap is the missing alarm, not the free space.

items.title: An unpushed RELEASE strands the successor — the lease handover is most fragile exactly when it happens
items.priority: P2 — cost is bounded and measured (16 min), but it recurs at EVERY handover
items.note:
⚠️ RE-HOMED FROM MI-86 BY THE MANAGER, 2026-09-03, BECAUSE THE ID WAS ALREADY TAKEN. The night manager filed this finding as MI-86 while MI-86 already existed on main as the night-shift handoff row -- so merging the branch as written would have SILENTLY DELETED that row, along with the finding main had since added to it (that a session-bound Routine fire reaches a RUNNING session, not only an IDLE one). Both rows survive: the handoff stays MI-86, this finding becomes MI-91. Nothing in the repo enforces id uniqueness across concurrent branches, and git cannot see the collision because to git it is just a changed value at the same key -- filed as its own defect.

FOUND BY LIVING IT, 2026-09-02. The night manager was spawned at 21:37:58Z and refused to manage for 16 minutes because origin said the lease was held. It was not: the day manager released it at 21:38:05Z, deliberately, with a note naming the incoming session. THE RELEASE REACHED origin ONLY AT 21:41:54Z (f19fd014, #10869). The successor fetched at 21:39:37Z — 2m17s inside that window — read 14f101eb, the last commit still showing state=held, and correctly stood down. ⚠️ THE GUARD WAS RIGHT AND SHOULD NOT BE WEAKENED. manager_preflight.py graded exactly what origin showed; a session must not manage on a lease it observes as held. The bug is the FRESHNESS OF THE FILE, never the strictness of the check. WHY IT IS STRUCTURAL, not bad luck: MANAGER-LEASE.json's own _doc warns about the unpushed window in the CLAIM direction ('a claim you never pushed protects nothing'). This is the SAME window in the RELEASE direction, where the cost is different — an unpushed release STRANDS THE SUCCESSOR. And it lands in the worst possible place: the outgoing manager releases and spawns its successor in the same breath, so the successor's very first read falls inside the window BY CONSTRUCTION. MEASURED COST: 16 minutes of night shift, plus a false accusation ('the spawn prompt lied') published to board #6927 and PR #10871 before the session re-read at 21:54Z and retracted it. The secondary lesson is the session's own: a NEGATIVE EXISTENCE CLAIM ('no release commit exists') from a single read of a store with a known unpushed window is not a measurement. CANDIDATE FIXES, NOT BUILT: (a) make `release --commit` push, or push the release BEFORE spawning the successor — the ordering is the whole bug and this is the cheap sufficient fix; (b) have manager_preflight.py re-fetch once on a held_fresh refusal and report 'held on origin as of <sha> at <time>' instead of bare 'held', so a stale read is VISIBLY stale — it currently reports state with no provenance for the read. NOT A FIX: telling sessions to trust the spawn prompt over the file. ⚠️ SECOND, INDEPENDENT WAY TO MISREAD THE SAME FILE, contributed by the outgoing day manager at 21:56Z and worth as much as the first: `manager_lease.py status` READS THE WORKING TREE, so running it while checked out on a FEATURE BRANCH reports that branch's copy of MANAGER-LEASE.json, not main's. The day manager reports this made IT briefly misreport the lease as HELD too. So there are now TWO distinct stale-read paths into the same wrong answer — a stale FETCH (this session's, the 2m17s window) and a stale CHECKOUT (any session standing on a branch). Both produce a confident, unqualified `held`. That strengthens fix (b) rather than replacing it: the tool should report WHERE and WHEN it read — 'held per <ref> at <sha>, read <time>' — because a reading with no provenance cannot be checked by the person it misleads. ⚠️ ALSO MEASURED: the day manager's correction was queued at 21:56:42Z and DELIVERED to this session at ~22:17Z — a ~20 MINUTE LAG, during which this session had already independently re-read the lease, claimed it, created the 05:00Z Routine and diagnosed MI-85. Cross-session correction is therefore NOT a reliable channel for unblocking a live session; the repo was the faster and more trustworthy one. That is an argument for putting corrections in the REGISTERS, which is where this session actually found them, rather than in messages.

Do not stretch the schema to fit -- that is the presence-only weakness the file's own header warns about. ⚠️ AND DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY GRADING ONLY THE NEWEST COMMIT: R6 exists precisely to catch a run of heartbeats made while supervision lapsed, and a last-commit-only rule would miss exactly that. The candidate shapes are (a) grade commits since the branch's last merge to main rather than since origin/main, or (b) let a REPAIR commit that brings SESSIONS.json current close out the earlier findings it repaired, recorded rather than silently forgiven. Both are design calls. DONE = a manager branch that has repaired its supervision record can go green on R6 WITHOUT the lapse being erased from the record, with a plant AND a control in --self-test.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THE DELIVERY: the escalation's only surface is a red workflow run and a line in a job log. It writes no pending-pings row, sends no Telegram, and raises no notification — so the page had been standing 17.4h across at least two scheduled runs (#7 21:19Z, #8 05:04Z) and reached nobody until a manager opened the job log by hand on 2026-09-04. A red run in a repo whose automation PRs are routinely red is invisible; that is the desensitised-alarm shape CLAUDE.md names as a P1 in its own right. ⚠️ WHAT IT WAS PAGING ABOUT WAS TRUE AND ACTIONABLE: 14 PRs waiting on a merge decision, worst 145.3h. ⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY MAKING THE RUN EXIT 0 — that removes the only signal there currently is. items.title: MERGE-QUEUE.json has no row-aware merge driver either, so the one register a CI rule enforces conflicts on every concurrent edit
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-04 while resolving #10977, which had gone `dirty`. With the row-aware driver ARMED, docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json and docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json auto-merged CLEANLY with zero hand editing; docs/claude/work/MERGE-QUEUE.json CONFLICTED and had to be resolved by hand. Cause is identical to MI-113: .gitattributes maps merge=jsonregister onto exactly five registers (health-review-backlog, OPEN-ITEMS, MANAGER-CHECKLIST, SESSIONS, OPEN-PRS) and MERGE-QUEUE.json is not among them -- `grep -c MERGE-QUEUE .gitattributes` returns 0. ⚠️ THIS IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE OF THE CLASS, not just another one: MERGE-QUEUE.json is the register whose invariant check_manager_scope R8 actively enforces, and the one the MANAGER rewrites several times a day by the queue duty. So the file most likely to be edited concurrently is one of the two with no driver. ⚠️ AND THE CONFLICT IS UNRESOLVABLE BY ITS AUTHOR: GitHub does not run custom merge drivers and update_pull_request_branch refuses, so a sub-session whose PR touches this file cannot free itself however attentive it is -- it needs someone with an armed clone. That is a queue-wide serialisation cost, not a cosmetic one. ⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT OBVIOUSLY THE SAME AS MI-113's. pending-pings.jsonl is append-only JSONL where `merge=union` may fit; MERGE-QUEUE.json is a small JSON object whose `entries` list is REPLACED wholesale by the manager rather than appended to, so a row-aware union could silently resurrect a queue entry the manager deliberately removed. Establish the right semantics before wiring a driver; a wrong driver here is worse than the conflict. Manager filed, did not build -- .gitattributes and scripts/ops/ are worker paths.

items.title: test_work_digest builds its control from the LIVE work store, so the whole suite goes red whenever in_flight legitimately reaches the ceiling
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-04, and it blocked the entire merge queue for ~90 minutes. tests/test_work_digest.py::test_ceiling_hit_is_loud_and_under_ceiling_is_not calls wd.build_digest('HEAD','HEAD') -- the REAL work store at the git ref -- and uses it as the NOT-HIT control: `assert 'WIP CEILING HIT' not in quiet`. So the control is only valid while production happens to be under the ceiling. The manager took in_flight to 8 of 8 at 07:43 by creating one work object -- a state scripts/ci/check_wip_ceiling.py explicitly grades `OK` -- and three tests went red on EVERY PR that runs the suite. ⚠️ THE CODE UNDER TEST WAS CORRECT THROUGHOUT. The digest was right to say WIP CEILING HIT; the ceiling WAS hit. The test asserts that production is not in a state production is allowed to be in. That is the inverse of the usual failure: not a green that checked nothing, but a RED that indicts nothing. ⚠️ IT IS INVISIBLE UNTIL IT BITES, for two reasons worth knowing. (1) pytest-run appears to be path-filtered: docs-only PRs completed it in 12-19s while PRs touching comms/ or src/ took 17-25min, so several manager landings merged green while the defect was already live. (2) The digest reads at a GIT REF, not the working tree, so a local fix does not take effect until it is COMMITTED -- the manager re-ran the tests after correcting the lifecycle, saw them still fail, and briefly concluded the diagnosis was wrong. HOW IT WAS IDENTIFIED, since the same reasoning finds the next one: #10919 is a PURE DATA ADDITION whose pytest-run PASSED on 2026-09-03 and failed on 2026-09-04 with no test change in its diff. A pure-data PR going red is the signal that the BASE moved, not the PR. ⚠️ MAIN'S OWN pytest-run RUNS ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF A GREEN BASE: they complete in 18-77s against a 17-25min PR run, so they are not running the suite. Do not clear this by pointing at them. THE FIX IS A SYNTHETIC FIXTURE for the control -- construct a store known to be under the ceiling rather than reading the live one. ⚠️ DO NOT 'fix' it by keeping in_flight below the ceiling: that makes an operational limit into a test constraint and hands every future manager a CI failure for using a documented allowance. Unblocked instead by correcting one object's stale lifecycle, on an operator decision, recorded in that object's lifecycle_note. || ROUTED 2026-09-05T03:43Z into the third and last slot (cap 3, now AT the cap, not over). items.title: manager-scope R7 picks its 'previous heartbeat' from the wrong lease run — a CLAIM over an expired lease is graded as a late check-in, and a merge reads sha~1's stale worker blob
items.note: TWO measured instances, ONE root, and the root is that R7 never establishes that the blob it compares against belongs to the same lease RUN, reached along the right parent. (a) MEASURED tonight on this manager's own re-claim commit cc984fec: R7 fails it at '746 minutes since this manager's previous heartbeat'. The 746 minutes are REAL and the failure is the point — the manager was idle twelve hours — but a CLAIM over an EXPIRED lease is a RECOVERY, not a late check-in, and R7's own docstring already exempts the sibling case: it compares only against 'a previous heartbeat by the SAME holder — a handover is not a lapse, and grading one would fail the incoming manager for the outgoing one's silence.' That reasoning transfers verbatim to a lease that DIED and was re-claimed. (b) The #10895 face, filed by MI-106's session rather than folded into its own PR (the correct disposition): R7 reads the previous blob from `sha~1`, which on a MERGE commit is the worker branch's stale lease, so merge 5244dafb reads as a lapse when the true same-holder gap was 49min, inside the 90min TTL — BL-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-R7-MEASURES-CADENCE-ALONG-THE-FIRST-PARENT-SO-A-MANAGER-MERGE-INTO-A-WORKER-BRANCH-READS-AS-A-LAPSE. ⚠️ THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION IS THE INCENTIVE, NOT THE RED: as written, the cheapest route to a green PR for a returning manager is to NOT PUSH THE LEASE — i.e. not record the lapse — while MANAGER-LEASE.json's own header says an unpushed claim protects nothing. A guard whose cheapest evasion is deleting the evidence is the new-table-wiring-guard shape this repo already names. ⚠️ OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-04, asked directly as a popup and answered 'Fix R7, route it to a session': fix the guard, do NOT write a manager-scope-exception entry, and accept that #10982 stays red until this lands. Recorded as a decision, not as a manager's own judgement. ⚠️ THE DEAD INTERVAL MUST STILL BE REPORTED. Reporting 746 minutes of no manager is the single most valuable thing the guard said tonight; what changes is where it is CHARGED, never whether it is SEEN — a silent pass here would be worse than tonight's false red. And R7's real case is untouched: a manager that is ALIVE and silent past one TTL must still fail. BLOCKS: #10982 (the manager register state, MI-118..MI-121, the session-cap resolution, and the record of the twelve-hour gap itself) and #10895. ⚠️ UPDATE 2026-09-04T23:44:07Z: MERGED as a0b776fa. ⚠️ THE DEADLOCK IS BROKEN AND IT WAS TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: the manager re-ran check_manager_scope.py --base origin/main on a fresh heartbeat commit under the corrected guard and got rc=0, verdict `unattributed` (one commit in range carries no Claude-Session trailer, which is the three-state grading MI-106 shipped and is not a violation). So the manager's lease heartbeat can now reach main, #10982 is unblocked, and #10895's own R7 face should clear too — that second half is NOT yet confirmed and must be checked against #10895 itself rather than inferred from this. ⚠️ CLOSED 2026-09-05T00:13:48Z: manager verified rc=0 directly on a fresh heartbeat commit; the identical shape graded ✗R6 ✗R7 before. items.title: a manager that stops acting is detected by nothing — bound idle with a durable wake
items.note: MEASURED, and the measurement is this manager: last act ~09:45Z, operator asked at 21:53Z. TWELVE HOURS against a standing directive of thirty minutes — twenty-four times the bar — and NOTHING NOTICED. Not a check, not a probe, not a Routine, not another session. ⚠️ THE MANAGER DID NOT DIE, and that is what makes this a different object from the reaper. It stayed alive and connected and simply stopped taking turns. Every mechanism here is aimed at DEATH (the lease's 90min TTL, time-based takeover, 'a session that dies cannot hand over') and death is the case already covered. ALIVE-AND-SILENT is covered by nothing. COST, measured: #10975 was GREEN at 15:02:46Z with the operator's Tier-2 approval ALREADY GIVEN and sat unmerged ~7h; all three sub-sessions were at need_input by 09:41Z each naming the ONE act it waited on, and MI-107's was a restart go-ahead already given; the lease sat expired 746 minutes, claimable by anyone and claimed by nobody; the manager branch went dirty against 28 commits. ⚠️ THE LEASE IS NOT A DETECTOR — it EXPIRES correctly, and nothing READS an expired lease and acts. ⚠️ NOR IS R7 — it grades a heartbeat only when a commit ADVANCES one, so a manager writing no commits is graded by nothing at all. Same distinction CLAUDE.md already draws for BL-20260903-THE-PR-QUEUE-WATCHER-CANNOT-SEE-A-TEN-MINUTE-STALL, where every gap was 15–35min while a green PR sat ten minutes and the operator noticed first. Tonight is that finding at 48x. ⚠️ OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-04, asked as a popup and answered 'A durable wake, so idle is bounded' — over a reaper and over building both. The reaper is real, complementary and DEFERRED, to be filed as its own row, not folded in. ⚠️ CREATING THE ROUTINE IS A DEPLOY, NOT THE DONE-CONDITION. The bar is an OBSERVED wake into a real session that then ACTS on something waiting — the same bar OI-20260902-DECISION-DRAIN-ROUTINE-DOES-NOT-EXIST sets for its own stage (4). CONSTRAINTS carried into the spawn: no minted credentials (operator, 2026-09-02, 'no minted tokens, ever'); no GitHub cron (work-digest fired 5x against 24 declared, probes ~4h50m late, #10845 already moved the digest off cron); and NO further reminder or checklist line — that instruction already exists, was read at session start, and produced the gap. ⚠️ UPDATE 2026-09-04T23:44:07Z: MERGED as 5f397509. Its delivery half was OBSERVED before the merge: at 23:09:19Z the wake fired into the manager session as an out-of-band turn and reported the lease 901 minutes stale — a true reading of origin/main that the manager's own reflex disputed, and the reading that exposed the heartbeat-never-reaches-main deadlock. ⚠️ MERGED IS NOT ARMED. The scheduling half needs the operator to create the Routine from the claude.ai Routines UI with the Claude Code Remote connector attached (create_trigger via MCP yields sessions with no mcp__* tools, which the poke step requires; `connectors` is refused for this org). The prompt is now ON MAIN at docs/claude/work/manager-wake-routine-prompt.md. Until it exists, the manager's cadence is a hand-rolled send_later poke, which is scaffolding and not the mechanism. ⚠️ 2026-09-05T00:13:48Z: session ARCHIVED, complete. ⚠️ ITS OWN CLOSING SUMMARY SAYS 'PR #1234' — that number is GARBLED and must not be propagated; the real PR is #11014, merged as 5f397509, verified by the manager against origin/main. That wording exists because the identical belief was WRONG on the sibling PR the same night: #10921 was queued on 'main is three days stale', main was in fact 23.8h NEWER, and performing the routed take would have rewound the probe register. The manager's dispatch there stated the direction as settled and scoped the re-measure to the ROW SET only; only the session re-measuring the premise anyway caught it. ⚠️ AND THE MANAGER HAS NOW BEEN WRONG IN THE REWIND DIRECTION TWICE IN ONE NIGHT — that take, and the wholesale cp -r that rewound five generated registers by up to 7.9h. #10398 is ITSELF a rewind judgement, so the manager taking it would be putting the least reliable judge on the case. The done condition requires a per-file population on BOTH sides and a POSITIVE CONTROL on the instrument, because a broken set-difference that reports nothing looks exactly like a correct one that finds nothing. ⚠️ #11017 shares this PR's title and the manager nearly closed #10398 as superseded by it — the dispatch says to check numbers, not titles.

items.title: Re-grade OPEN-ITEMS loudness against a stated bar — 43 of 54 rows are loud:true — OPERATOR-APPROVED 2026-09-05
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-05, asked as a popup and answered 'Re-grade loudness against a bar'. MEASURED 2026-09-05T11:09Z: docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json holds 54 items and 43 carry loud:true — 79.6%. A flag that fires on four rows in five is not a priority signal, and every status update is obliged to carry all 43. That is the desensitized-alarm failure this repo names as its own P1 in CLAUDE.md's 'If you see something, say something' — the motivating incident there was a dataset audit that degenerated to 62/86 manifests alarming while a real bug soaked inside the noise for weeks. ⚠️ THE JOB IS TO DEFINE THE BAR FIRST AND GRADE AGAINST IT, NOT TO PICK A TARGET COUNT: deciding 'loud should be about ten rows' and trimming to fit is choosing the answer before the question. A defensible bar is something like money-at-risk, or a live gate that is ARMED but never exercised. ⚠️ EVERY RE-GRADE MUST RECORD ITS BASIS ON THE ROW, so a later session can tell a row that was assessed and found quiet from one nobody looked at — 'we did not look' and 'we looked and found nothing' are different facts and collapsing them is the exact class this repo guards against elsewhere. ⚠️ DEMOTING A ROW IS NOT CLOSING IT: loudness governs REPORTING, not whether the item is open. Nothing gets cleared by this pass.

items.title: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE: no session works without ownership, in any case — measured 0 of 79 idle sessions have a live owner
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, 2026-09-05, verbatim: "no sessions working on their own without ownership. That should not happen in any case." Given after the manager reported 79 idle sessions carried over from previous managers. || MEASURED THE SAME DAY, platform truth joined to SESSIONS.json, population = the 79 sessions the platform reports IDLE: ZERO have an owner session that is currently RUNNING; 76 are ORPHANED (their spawned_by is itself idle/archived/dead); 1 records no spawned_by at all; 2 are NOT IN THE REGISTRY AT ALL; and 32 name NEITHER a checklist_item NOR an owns_object, so you could not tell what they were for even having found them. The only RUNNING session account-wide was the manager. || ⚠️ THE ENFORCEMENT CANNOT BE BUILT ON THE CURRENT REGISTER. Before the same-day re-grade, 65 of 94 rows carried a state the platform contradicts and 58 had never been observed once, so the register claimed 41 sessions were working/idle/running. Ownership derived from a store that is 69% wrong about state inherits the lie — derive it at READ time from a live list_sessions join, the same fix `state` needs. || ⚠️ WHAT WOULD NOT SATISFY THIS: archiving the 79 (resolves lifecycle, says NOTHING about whether their work reached main — an idle session is not a finished one); or a documented rule that managers must register and check ownership, which is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix MI-15 has already failed three times with the recorded remedy 'remember to register'. || THE MANAGER DID NOT BUILD THIS (worker item: scripts/**) AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT SWEEP-ARCHIVE THE 79, which would have destroyed the evidence the item rests on.
